readout_other: CRS-R; resting EEG delta/beta ratio; 18F-FDG PET SUV; polysomnography (Dreem 2 headband); Disability Rating Scale
direction_notes: Maximum CRS-R total score and EEG delta/beta ratio increased after tFUS, and glucose metabolism decreased bilaterally in thalamus and frontal, temporal and parietal cortices; authors describe a convergent inhibitory signature.
safety_notes: No severe adverse events; two events during the stay (urinary tract infection, hypotension) were judged unrelated to the intervention by an independent medical monitor.

timing.protocol_description: Sonication was administered in 20 blocks of 30 s, with 30 s rest intervals in between, for a total of 10 minutes of (non-continuous) cumulative sonication, at a PRF of 100 Hz and a pulse width of 0.5 ms. Single session; transducers with 55 mm or 65 mm focal depth chosen per patient.

source_quotes.n_subjects: The average $\mathrm { C R S - R } _ { \operatorname* { m a x } }$ across the full enrolled population at baseline (N=16) was 10.25 (SD = 2.49).
source_quotes.n_sessions_per_subject: Methods Sixteen adult patients (44% Female; Age, M=37.81, SD=15.97) with a chronic DOC (Time Since Injury, M=3.39, SD=1.94 years) secondary to severe brain injury (TBI 44%, non-TBI 56%) underwent a 10-day inpatient, longitudinal, single-arm, open-label protocol. tFUS was delivered in a single session targeting the left central thalamus.
source_quotes.exposures[0].fundamental_frequency_khz: tFUS was delivered with a Brainsonix BX Pulsar 1002 device, operating at a fundamental frequency of 650 kHz, with a 61 mm curvature diameter piezoelectric element, a radial focus of approximately 0.25 cm and a longitudinal focal spread of \~1.25 cm.<sup>50</sup> To accommodate patientspecific neuroanatomy (e.g., degree of ventricular enlargement), transducers with different focal depths were employed (55 mm and 65 mm focal depth transducers) as determined by measuring, on a T1-weighted MRI, the distance from the thalamic target to the exterior portion of the temporal bone at its thinnest position.
